title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the functional equation of the L-function L_E(t) of an ℓ-adic sheaf (or similar coefficient system) E on a curve over F_q, possibly non-proper, in the cohomological formalism. Here δ(E) is the constant (determinant of Frobenius) and χ(E) the Euler characteristic. The 'equation above' is not on this page; it seems to have the form L_E(1/(qt)) = A(t) δ(E) (-t)^{χ(E)} L_E(t). A(t) is a correction built from local factors L^∞_E at the points at infinity. From the next line it appears that A(t) = L^∞_E(1/(qt))^{-1}, or something equivalent.

Step 1. Set B(t) = A(t) δ(E)(-t)^{χ(E)}, so that L(1/(qt)) = B(t) L(t).

Step 2. Apply the involution t ↦ 1/(qt) to this equation. This gives L(t) = B(1/(qt)) L(1/(qt)) = B(1/(qt)) B(t) L(t). Hence B(t) B(1/(qt)) = 1, the consistency (cocycle) condition for an involutive functional equation.

Step 3. Substitute the value of B. The factors combine as (-t)^χ (-1/(qt))^χ = q^{-χ}. This gives L^∞_E(1/(qt))^{-1} δ(E)(-t)^χ · L^∞_E(t)^{-1} δ(E)(-1/(qt))^χ = 1. Equivalently, L^∞_E(t) L^∞_E(1/(qt)) = δ(E)^2 q^{-χ(E)}. Grothendieck notes that this is exactly the functional equation for the local factor at infinity made explicit earlier, so the global equation is self-consistent.

Step 4. Pass to a symmetrized form. Put ξ_E(t) = t^{χ(E)/2} L_E(t). Then ξ_E(1/(qt)) = (qt)^{-χ/2} A(t) δ(E)(-t)^χ L_E(t) = q^{-χ/2} A(t) δ(E)(-1)^χ ξ_E(t). This is the analogue of the completed ξ-function with s ↔ 1-s symmetry; the page ends mid-sentence ('i.e.').

All of this is a formal verification. It serves the broader project in this file: writing the functional equation of geometric L-functions with local factors at infinity, in the style of Weil and of SGA 5 / Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk.

Note: the neighbouring 'pages' are typed Bourbaki drafts (Commutative Algebra ch. VII, n° 392). They are evidently the rectos of the scrap paper Grothendieck wrote on, and are unrelated to this page's content.
errors: No mathematical error. The exponent bookkeeping is correct: (-t)^χ(-1/(qt))^χ = q^{-χ} and (qt)^{-χ/2}(-t)^χ = (-1)^χ q^{-χ/2} t^{χ/2}.
The machine transcription's extra factor '1/t' in δ(E)^2 (1/t) q^{-χ(E)} must be spurious (a scribble or crossed mark). The correct right-hand side is δ(E)^2 q^{-χ(E)}, with no t-dependence.

ideas.what: Consistency (involution) condition B(t)B(1/(qt)) = 1 for a functional equation L(1/(qt)) = B(t)L(t)
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle/compatibility condition for the functional equation under s ↦ 1-s
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (folklore; Weil, Tate for local/global compatibility)
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in SGA 5 / Bourbaki exposé 279 discussion of the functional equation

ideas.what: Functional equation for the local factor at infinity, L^∞_E(t)L^∞_E(1/(qt)) = δ(E)^2 q^{-χ(E)}, deduced from the global one
ideas.modern_name: Local functional equation for local L-factors/ε-factors at the boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (local), Deligne/Laumon (local constants in the function-field case)

ideas.what: Completed function ξ_E(t) = t^{χ(E)/2} L_E(t) giving a symmetric functional equation
ideas.modern_name: Completed L-function / symmetric form of the Grothendieck–Lefschetz functional equation

deep.surprise_reason: Routine algebraic check of an involutive functional equation and its symmetrization. It is standard material and not new relative to SGA 4½/SGA 5 or Laumon's work on local constants.
transcription_corrections: 'A(t)δ(E)χ(-t)^{χ(E)} = B(t)' should read 'A(t)δ(E)(-t)^{χ(E)} = B(t)'; the stray χ is an artifact.
The right-hand side 'δ(E)^2 \frac{1}{t} q^{-χ(E)}' should be 'δ(E)^2 q^{-χ(E)}'. The mark before q is a scribble or correction, not 1/t.
'récrit[?] par p^nζ = q [?]' is illegible in the image. It is likely an aside fixing q as a power of p (e.g. 'où ... p^n = q'), not a substantive formula.
The crossed-out word after 'en' is 'substituant', replaced by 'posant'.
The line beginning 'L^∞_E(1/(qt))^{-1} δ(E)(-t)^{χ(E)} ...' has a crossed-out 'q' in the denominator; the intended argument is 1/(qt).
